title: Designing for the Real World
context: Situational impairments, including glare, sunlight, fatigue, and motion
whyItMatters: A screen designed in a controlled room can become difficult to read outdoors or while someone is moving.
learningObjectives: Understand how ambient sunlight reduces screen visibility.
Identify how movement can affect reading precision.
lessonParagraphs: People use mobile devices in changing environments, not only at a desk with steady lighting. The context can temporarily restrict someone's ability to see or interact with a device, creating a situational impairment.
Direct sunlight can overpower the light emitted by a phone display. As ambient light increases, perceived screen contrast drops, and text that relies on subtle grays can wash out.
Movement, noise, and temperature can also affect interaction. Walking divides attention and can reduce reading comprehension, motor accuracy, and visual stability.
Strong contrast helps a design handle changing light and motion. It can support a transition from a dim room to a bright, moving environment.

optionalArticle.title: Challenges of Situational Impairments during Interaction with Mobile Devices
optionalArticle.author: Zhanna Sarsenbayeva

keyTakeaways: Environments can create temporary situational impairments.
Bright sunlight can wash out screen contrast.
Strong contrast helps designs handle unpredictable lighting and motion.
internalNote: Situational impairments are not formally evaluated by automated tools.
